result:
**Verdict: accept.** No concrete blockers in this delta.

**CI timeout 20 to 35 minutes.** This is a whole-job wall-clock cap, not one of the enforced budgets in AGENTS.md. The startup budget step and per-test limits are untouched, so nothing this project actually guards against regressing has been loosened. With tests plus build at about 16 minutes and the npm and release smokes after that, 35 leaves sensible headroom on the slower Node 20 runner without hiding a hang.

**Bootstrap override in the ready-path fixture.** The change is correct in kind. A fixture named as fully mocked was reaching the live registry, so it was non-hermetic and would fail for any unpublished workspace package, not just this one. Setting the bootstrap check to ok restores the fixture to what it claimed to be. The negative behavior you care about is still asserted by the product-entry-cli regression, which checks that a missing package flips npm readiness to false, emits the bootstrap error check with the missing package listed, and prints the bootstrap next step. The real release doctor path is unchanged, so an actual publish attempt still blocks on the unpublished graph package.

**Two non-blocking notes.**

- The accept assumes the CI re-run with this diff goes green. The smoke failure was reproduced locally and fixed with the same env var, and the change is a deterministic env override, so I do not expect a difference, but the run cited in your summary predates the fix.
- The fixture now hard-codes every external check to ok. If a future check is added without a corresponding override, the smoke will again silently query a live service. Consider a follow-up that fails the fixture when any release check lacks an explicit test override, but that is outside this delta.
